Found: initGrid() in useSinglePlayerCore.ts runs pickRichestBoardClient synchronously on the main thread before the board can paint -- it generates k candidate boards via generateTableWithEmbeddedWords (up to 5 placement attempts x ~12-25 words x up to 100 placement tries each) and scores each, blocking the game grid's first paint. k=6 was an unjustified magic default paying 2x the necessary synchronous cost for a 'best of N' board-quality heuristic that degrades gracefully at lower N. Halving to k=3 cuts this blocking work ~2x for every single-player board generation (bots autostart, practice, warmup, adventure, results-page replay, earthquake fire-round -- all share this one function), not just the noisy route in tonight's brief.
